title: Specify human semantic and assistive-technology review gates
description:
## Goal

Specify review evidence states and escalation for semantic correctness and assistive-technology checks; do not claim that a machine pass replaces either gate. Standards, tools, sampling and sign-off authority remain open.

## Plan

Use only synthetic or deidentified fixtures. This is planning/decomposition; the test cases are specifications, not executed product tests. Follow red/green/refactor for any later code work.

## Test cases

TC-REM-HUMAN-001, TC-REM-ASSISTIVE-TECH-001, TC-GEN-VALIDATION-001

## Definition of done

Acceptance case IDs are present in the traceability catalog with Given/When/Then outcomes; implementation does not begin while listed decision gates remain unresolved.
acceptance_criteria: Refinement readiness: refinement-ready. Cover only the named test case IDs: TC-REM-HUMAN-001, TC-REM-ASSISTIVE-TECH-001, TC-GEN-VALIDATION-001. Keep unresolved profiles/feasibility as blockers; report unsupported or ambiguous cases explicitly. No implementation result is claimed by this issue.
close_reason: Case specifications and traceability are recorded in docs/traceability/catalog.json and generated docs/validation/cases.md. Planning checker and integrity tests pass; these are specifications only, not product tests or implementation results.

title: Independent remediation validation and release gates
description: Define layered release gates for remediation outputs: independent machine validation, semantic correctness review by a human, and assistive-technology review. Include failure classification and traceable audit evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: define failing validator-fixture tests, false-positive/false-negative handling, accessibility tree checks, and human review checklist cases before wiring gates. Include veraPDF as a candidate machine-only validator, not proof of WCAG conformance. DoD: machine checks do not replace human semantic or assistive-technology gates; tagged output alone is never called PDF/UA or WCAG compliant.

title: Build synthetic characterization and gold fixture plan
description: Define a versioned synthetic/deidentified fixture corpus and characterization strategy for existing PDFs across statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports. Capture expected input behavior and preservation constraints before remediation changes.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: author fixture manifests and failing characterization assertions before any writer or repair code. Cover visible text, layout, page count, reading order where known, links/forms/annotations where applicable, language and metadata. Include malformed, scanned, and mixed-content cases only as synthetic fixtures. DoD: fixture provenance and safe handling are documented; never migrate prior private reports or sample documents.

title: Define document data, accessibility, and security profiles
description: Inventory the profile decisions that affect processing and acceptance: statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports; source data fields; language; confidentiality; retention; accessibility expectations; and human review needs. Use synthetic/deidentified examples only. Keep unresolved choices explicitly proposed.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: define profile schema examples and invalid/ambiguous cases, then assert validation behavior in contract tests. Include representative examples for all four document families. Red/green/refactor the schema and docs; record decisions and unresolved owner questions. DoD: no real sample documents or private reports; fixture and threat-data handling rules are documented.
notes:
2026-10-12 Phase 0: added generation and remediation profile schemas with four synthetic family examples per lane. internal/profile validates explicit proposed/open fields and invalid or ambiguous cases; profile tests pass. Evidence: docs/profiles/README.md and internal/profile. Language, source-field policy, confidentiality, retention, and review authority remain open; PDF/UA-2 is the accepted output target per docs/decisions/0001-pdf-ua-2-validation-target.md. Semantic policy and conformance evidence remain open; keep this gate in progress.
2026-10-12 follow-up: Added test-first validation for canonical source-field identifiers: rejects leading/trailing whitespace and duplicate canonical names. This leaves profile values and unresolved policy choices unchanged. Focused go test -race ./internal/profile ./internal/pdfua and go vet ./internal/profile ./internal/pdfua pass. Added HTTPS-only source publication guidance preserving CloudBot identity; underlying credential provider remains unverified. This is a narrow engineering slice; profile task remains in progress and no phase or conformance gate is closed.
2026-10-12 review follow-up: Aligned generation/remediation JSON Schema boundary checks with Go strings.TrimSpace Unicode whitespace (including U+0085, NBSP, Unicode spaces, LF/CR); FEFF remains accepted at boundaries because Go does not trim it. Tests assert the distinct padded-name and duplicate-canonical-name errors. JSON Schema uniqueItems limitation is documented; no duplicate-after-trimming test is claimed. title: Existing-PDF writer and fidelity feasibility spike
description:
Probe whether an open-source PDF writer can preserve the required existing-PDF structures and visible fidelity while adding/remapping accessibility structure. Evaluate Apache-2.0 PDFBox as a candidate alongside alternatives. Scope this as a Go adapter feasibility question, not a Go PDF library assumption. Use synthetic/deidentified gold fixtures covering the four families.

## Goal

Run a bounded, test-first feasibility investigation using synthetic or safely sourced non-confidential fixtures.

## Findings

Pending the spike. Record reproducible observations, exact versions and licenses, limitations, and an evidence-backed recommendation before closing this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: before implementation, define characterization snapshots and preservation assertions for visible text, page geometry/rendering, links, forms, annotations, fonts, and metadata as applicable. Run a minimal writer round-trip spike, measure fixture diffs only (no invented target), document failure modes, licensing, and a go/no-go decision. No production writer is selected until this gate passes.
notes:
2026-10-12 Phase 0: pinned pdfcpu v0.16.2 (Apache-2.0, source tag commit b41a41d) and added a full-write round-trip harness for synthetic statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports. Tests cover page geometry, decoded content, font, links, widget/form value, /P and /Pg references, /Stm MCR, OBJR, and sparse ParentTree null hole. Workspace Poppler checks also matched text, tag-tree view, link and 72-DPI rendered PNG pixels. Producer and timestamps change. Evidence: internal/pdfpreserve/roundtrip_test.go and docs/research/pdfcpu-v0.16.2.md. Multi-page/complex inputs and a full transitive/runtime review remain open; no production writer selected.
2026-10-12 follow-up: added and red/green-validated a two-leaf nested /Pages fixture (SHA-256 183acc6a424d9a62e85e811b87129f2b8b6aab48ec2621ab3804899aeca29196). Root declares MediaBox [0 0 612 792] and Rotate 270; nested node declares CropBox [18 24 594 768] and overriding Rotate 90; both leaves inherit the effective values and carry distinct content streams. Full-write round trip preserves effective MediaBox/CropBox/Rotate, per-page content, page count, and input bytes. Independent negative controls changing the nested CropBox and Rotate were initially accepted by the comparator, then failed after adding effective-attribute assertions. Test: TestFullWriteRoundTripPreservesNestedPageTreeInheritance and TestNestedPageTreeRoundTripRejectsInheritedCropBoxAndRotateMutations. Full suite with -race, vet, go mod tidy -diff, and traceability passed on baseline 9bb9f2a202632fa92359d288ab298853c89434e7 with Go 1.27.2. Evidence in internal/pdfpreserve/roundtrip_test.go and docs/research/pdfcpu-v0.16.2.md. Limits: synthetic-only, no renderer, no tags/fonts/forms/annotations, arbitrary depth, invalid rotations, third-party corpus, semantic correctness or PDF/UA claim. Writer remains unselected; keep this spike in progress pending broader acceptance evidence.
2026-10-12 independent-review correction: strengthened the nested-page-tree fixture with an explicit empty /Resources <<>> on nested /Pages object 3. Added an assertion that both leaves omit /Resources and their nearest ancestor supplying it is object 3, and that the full-write output retains an empty effective resource dictionary. Go-first red: the new assertion rejected the prior fixture because object 3 lacked /Resources. Green fixture SHA-256 is now 1b5060daf940c0591deaf91ecab8d8d704c1bfc3d02fdaebfd1630d430de170d; focused round-trip and CropBox/Rotate mutation controls pass. Evidence and limits in docs/research/pdfcpu-v0.16.2.md. The spike remains in progress.
2026-10-12 final fixture-validity correction: asserted catalog /Pages reference; root and nested /Pages /Type, /Kids, and /Count 2; root MediaBox/Rotate; nested Parent/CropBox/Rotate/empty Resources; and both leaf /Page types, parents, and content references. Go-first red exposed missing nested /Count. Restored it and updated the inline fixture SHA-256 to 0111496f4c411a67040217882c5cf26fc9819b994b0792290dd783a35794859c. Renamed the test to TestFullWriteRoundTripPreservesNestedPageEffectiveAttributes. The source hierarchy is validated, but output topology is intentionally unconstrained; only effective inherited geometry/resources and per-page content are compared. Focused nested round-trip and CropBox/Rotate negative controls pass.

title: Authenticate veraPDF 1.30.3 and establish genuine PDF/UA-2 oracle controls
description:
## Goal

Authenticate the official veraPDF CLI artifact and establish genuine PDF/UA-2 pass/finding oracle controls for the CI-only integration.

## Plan

Use only the official installer route. Verify the exact artifact signer key/fingerprint and detached signature, compute and pin local SHA-256 digests for the signed installer and installed CLI JAR, and record the CI-only MPL-2.0 election after bundled notice inspection. Force `--flavour ua2`; no auto-detection or fallback. Use genuine upstream PDF/UA-2 controls with provenance and hashes.

## Evidence

The official `software.verapdf.org` installer, signature, and key endpoints returned HTTP 200 in the fresh environment. The signing key primary fingerprint matched the value published in official veraPDF installation documentation; GPG verified the exact installer signature. Installer and CLI JAR SHA-256 pins, route evidence, license notices, control provenance, and actual CLI output are recorded in `docs/research/verapdf-cli-1.30.3.md`.

The Go adapter runs the authenticated CLI against official corpus pass/finding controls and rejects a tampered copy of the pinned CLI JAR. Fake-process tests continue to cover operational failures. All results are machine-only and do not imply semantic or assistive-technology approval.

## Test cases

TC-PDFUA2-REAL-ORACLE-001 and TC-REM-MACHINE-001.

## Definition of done

The pinned official signature/hash checks, explicit UA-2 CLI invocation, and genuine pass/finding controls pass in the dedicated CI workflow and the changes receive independent PR review. A human semantic/assistive-technology release gate remains separate. Do not close parent issue `dap-jo9.2.5` based on this machine-only evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The exact official installer signature and primary signer fingerprint are verified against official documentation; installer and installed CLI SHA-256 values are pinned; the CI-only MPL-2.0 boundary and bundled notices are documented; the pinned CLI proves explicit ua2 profile selection against genuine upstream pass/finding controls; artifact tampering and operational failure behavior are covered; independent PR review and required CI pass. Human semantic and assistive-technology review remain separate, and parent dap-jo9.2.5 stays open.

title: Implement CI-only PDF/UA-2 validator adapter
description:
## Goal
Add a Go-only subprocess adapter contract for independent PDF/UA-2 validation, usable from CI and tests. The adapter is not a product runtime integration.

## Plan
Use red/green/refactor with fake-process tests first. Pin the requested profile explicitly with --flavour ua2; never allow auto-detection or PDF/UA-1/PDF/A fallback. Bound runtime and output, isolate temp inputs, classify validator exit codes, and fail closed on malformed/missing/mismatched XML reports. No real-PDF fixture may be called known-pass/fail until validated by an authenticated veraPDF release.

## Test cases
TC-REM-MACHINE-001 and TC-GEN-VALIDATION-001, plus adapter-only synthetic report contract cases.

## Definition of done
Go tests cover compliant/noncompliant XML, profile mismatch, malformed/missing reports, process failure, timeout and output cap using fake processes. Documentation labels reports synthetic and keeps human semantic/assistive-technology review as mandatory. Real veraPDF execution, actual PDF/UA-2 oracle fixtures, and any conformance conclusion remain blocked pending authenticated official artifact acquisition and human review.
acceptance_criteria: Test first: fake-process contract tests pass for explicit ua2 profile, valid compliant and noncompliant reports, wrong profile, malformed or missing reports, exit/report mismatch, timeout, output cap, and isolated temp cleanup. The parser must reject duplicate attributes, namespace shadowing, absent or empty required numeric counters, and malformed reports without exposing input tokens in errors. Relative TempDir values must yield absolute subprocess artifact/input paths and clean up correctly. The adapter is test/CI-only, bounded, fail-closed, and covered against authenticated real pass/finding oracle controls. No semantic accessibility or certification claim follows from machine validation.
notes:
2026-10-12 TDD adapter implementation started on ua2/preparation. Synthetic fake-process tests now pass for ua2 args, copied temp input, compliant/noncompliant report classification, profile mismatch, malformed/missing XML, exit/report disagreement, processing exit code, input/output caps, and timeout. This is adapter-shim evidence only; no veraPDF process or PDF conformance fixture has been validated. Official signing-key URL returned proxy 403; Maven Central JAR reachable but guessed detached-signature/checksum sidecars absent. Keep real validator and oracle controls blocked.
2026-10-12 follow-up: review of the official v1.30.3 CLI XML guide/source corrected the parser to require a report root containing exactly one job and one validationReport with the exact UA-2 profileName. Result carries CLI version and candidate SHA-256. Tests now also cover truncated reports, multiple jobs, unavailable executable, cancellation, and temp cleanup. `go test -race ./internal/pdfua ./internal/profile ./internal/devsecops ./internal/traceability` passes. Earlier note saying Maven signature/checksum sidecars absent was based on malformed URL suffixes; corrected research confirms correct .jar.asc/.jar.sha256 URLs are reachable. Their signer is still unauthenticated until official key route is available.
2026-10-12 follow-up 2: verified official CLI XML shape and tightened fail-closed parser to validate one report/job/validationReport plus one batchSummary, processing-error counters, and summary/report consistency. Fake-process tests now bound aggregate stdout+stderr bytes. Synthetic samples remain parser-only, explicitly not veraPDF output or conformance evidence.
2026-10-12 review fixes: start the deadline before input/artifact preparation; use Linux O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK plus regular-file checks to reject symlinks/FIFOs; fail closed on non-Linux. Linux adapter runs the validator in its own process group, signals the whole group on cancellation, and sets bounded WaitDelay. Regression test exits the process-group leader while a descendant holds stdout/stderr, then checks bounded return, descendant reaping, and temp cleanup. XML parser rejects non-whitespace before/after the single report root and requires all summary attributes used for classification. Public errors redact input/artifact paths. Focused race tests and vet pass. Full suite remains blocked on pdfcpu module proxy 403; no real veraPDF artifact or integration verified. Issue remains in progress pending review.
2026-10-12 PR #7 independent-review follow-up: TDD regressions confirmed duplicate classification attribute rejection, namespace/default-namespace shadowing rejection, empty required numeric counters, content-free malformed XML errors, and relative TempDir handling. Parser now scans XML tokens for duplicate attrs/namespaces and returns generic errors, validates counters as exact required strings, and normalizes the isolated temp directory to an absolute path. Real veraPDF controls remain covered by the authenticated integration test.
2026-10-12 completion evidence: PR #7 was independently approved and merged. Exact reviewed head d1906d49a46f4fc2b675bd5274b413df442833e1; merge commit 591b20e6c318f05baa5f871a48b90d27255d32dd. Red/green review regressions against pre-fix c8e1a5b confirmed unsafe-then-safe duplicate compliance, failedToParse, and summary counters were accepted; all duplicate orderings now reject with a generic token-free XML report error. Required PR contexts and post-merge Go, go-security, secrets, dependency review, Analyze (go), Analyze (actions), CodeQL push scan, and pdfua2 completed successfully. Local go test -race ./... -count=1, go vet ./..., go mod tidy -diff, and traceability passed. This closes only the adapter task; machine validation does not satisfy semantic, human, or assistive-technology gates.
close_reason: Adapter implementation and hardening merged in PR #7 at 591b20e6c318f05baa5f871a48b90d27255d32dd; required checks and post-merge validation passed. Semantic and human/AT gates remain separate.

title: Implement first DevSecOps scanner and policy tranche
description:
## Goal

Implement the approved first tranche of repository-local DevSecOps checks: pinned Go vulnerability and license scans, focused workflow/config policy regression tests, and full-history secret scanning with safe redaction.

## Plan

Use maintained permissive tools and pinned upstream Actions/releases. Keep existing PDF dependencies test-only and unapproved for runtime. Preserve read-only workflow tokens and credential-free checkouts. Do not modify GitHub settings or branch rules, install hooks, or add optional PDF runtimes. Use TDD and synthetic-only scanner fixtures.

## Test cases

Cover scanner finding/failure/error behavior; immutable Action pins, least-privilege permissions and expected triggers; structured secret exceptions with expiry, owner and Beads reference; clean/finding/error/config outcomes for Gitleaks; test-inclusive vulnerability and license scans; actionlint; full-history Gitleaks with redacted findings.

## Definition of done

Pinned workflows run on pull requests and main, with periodic vulnerability checks. License policy is explicit, reviewed, and fails on unknown or unapproved licenses including test dependencies. Regression tests prove both pass and failure paths. Secret exceptions are narrowly scoped to synthetic fixtures and require expiry, owner, and Beads issue. Docs describe triggers, redaction, exception process, current CodeQL setup, and remaining gates. No new account permissions/security settings or production integrations are introduced.
acceptance_criteria: DoD: pinned scans run on PRs to main and main pushes with weekly vulnerability checks; Go policy tests cover fail-closed scanner invocation, SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege permissions and triggers; Gitleaks scans full history with verified redacted output and structured synthetic-only exceptions; docs record tool behavior and CodeQL execution distinction; local tests and GitHub CI results are recorded; no settings, branch rules, real documents, hooks or runtime integrations are changed.
notes:
Implementation in progress on branch devsecops/first-tranche. Added least-privilege scanner workflow, test-inclusive vulnerability and license checks, SHA-pinned Actions, redacted full-history Gitleaks with SHA-verified official release archive, synthetic smoke script, exception policy tests, and security operations docs. Local go test -race ./... and go vet ./... pass. Scanner binary execution remains pending CI because this environment blocks upstream module asset downloads.
GitHub CI verified the pinned Gitleaks release SHA-256 and exposed that the common synthetic AWS sample is excluded by the scanner. Replaced it with an ephemeral custom-rule fixture and redaction assertions; awaiting rerun.
Second CI attempt confirmed the synthetic rule detects the fixture; the text-output assertion was incompatible with current CLI output. Smoke test now checks the temporary redacted JSON report for the expected path/rule and confirms the synthetic value is absent.
Final GitHub CI on PR #1 passed: go-security (policy/project tests, vet, actionlint, test-inclusive govulncheck, test-inclusive go-licenses), secrets (SHA-verified Gitleaks archive, clean/finding/redaction/config smoke checks, full-history scan), existing Go checks, dependency review, and default CodeQL Go/Actions analyses. The synthetic smoke fixture needed two CI-driven fixes; the final run is green.
Reopened after independent review found gaps in Gitleaks suppression governance, license/actionlint scanner policy tests, and live exception expiry date handling. Fixes and revalidation in progress.
Scoped independent-review fixes added locally: explicit default-only Gitleaks config and /dev/null ignore-path policy with synthetic controls for both suppression mechanisms; license/actionlint invocation guards plus a test-only forbidden-license smoke module; live registry expiry now uses current UTC date. Local race tests and vet pass; GitHub validation/re-review pending.

title: Isolate pinned security scanners from PR-controlled tests
description:
## Problem

PR-controlled Go tests run before later security scanner commands and can replace executables in the same writable Go install directory.

## Steps to Reproduce

In a temporary module, install a dummy scanner in GOBIN, run a Go test that overwrites it, then invoke the scanner by name. The invocation resolves to the replacement.

## Expected Behavior

Untrusted test code cannot replace or shadow the pinned scanner used by later CI steps. Separate scanner execution from PR-controlled tests or use an immutable trusted scanner path. Do not increase token permissions.
acceptance_criteria: Structure scanner execution so PR-controlled tests cannot overwrite or shadow installed scanner binaries (for example, isolate scan and test jobs or use an immutable trusted scanner path). A fixture Go test that attempts to replace or shadow a scanner must not change which binary later scan commands execute. Keep least-privilege permissions.
close_reason: Scanner execution was isolated from PR-controlled Go tests with policy regression coverage. PR #17 merged at edd03607d408124bd8284a9c5e8ef948e66f00bc after all 9 required checks passed. Least-privilege permissions are preserved.

title: Bind validator evidence to staged bytes and reject output errors
description:
## Problem

The CI runner records a pre-copy candidate digest and can accept output-sink failures as the expected validator finding exit.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use an install wrapper to change a copied control after sha256sum and a Docker shim to record the staged bytes. Separately, emit valid noncompliant XML followed by whitespace until the 8 MiB cap and exit 1; verify the resulting contract with TestVerifyDownloadedCIControlBundles. Repeat with valid stdout plus stderr overflow.

## Expected Behavior

The staged bytes must match the recorded candidate digest. At/above-limit output and Docker stdout/stderr write failures must not produce a known-finding bundle accepted by the Go verifier. Keep real validator execution in authenticated CI.
acceptance_criteria: In a disposable test harness, verify staged candidate digest matches the value in the contract after copy. Reject output at or above the configured byte limit and Docker client/output sink errors on stdout or stderr even when the report prefix is valid. Ensure operational failures cannot be classified as the expected noncompliant validator finding; real CLI execution stays in the authenticated CI job.
notes:
Implementation evidence: staged digest recheck, combined output cap, sink handling, incomplete-pipe/process-tree cleanup, and Docker shims pass locally. Acceptance pending independent final review and remote PR CI; no remote CI ran because draft PR creation returned Forbidden. Real veraPDF controls remain CI-only and have not run locally.
2026-10-12 acceptance reconciliation: The preceding pending-review/remote-CI text records the pre-merge state and is historical. PR #16 reviewed head bda0c7b passed all 9 required checks; merge commit 4760735eb957d1081922a00bff7cfc93c7b90020 passed all 7 post-merge checks, including validator-container and pdfua2 with authenticated controls. Acceptance is complete for this CI hardening child; real validator controls remain CI-only.
close_reason: Staged-byte digest recheck, shared output cap, sink-failure handling, bounded process-tree/pipe cleanup, and Docker regressions pass. title: Compare raw PDF stream bytes in preservation checks
description:
## Problem

The round-trip comparator misses encoded Raw stream mutations when pdfcpu uses its default DecodeAllStreams=false setting.

## Steps to Reproduce

Create the synthetic statement PDF, read independent baseline and writer contexts, mutate same-length Raw bytes in object 13 or 14, write and reread the PDF, then call compareRoundTrip. The comparator currently returns nil although the serialized Raw bytes changed.

## Expected Behavior

The preservation comparator must detect encoded content changes for both the page content stream and form XObject. This is characterization evidence only, not PDF/UA conformance.
acceptance_criteria: Add TDD controls that mutate same-length Raw bytes in object 13 and object 14 before writing; compareRoundTrip must reject each mutation against an independently read baseline. Existing round-trip characterization and race tests pass. Document that this is fidelity evidence, not PDF/UA conformance.
notes:

title: Fail closed when Gitleaks suppression discovery fails
description:
## Problem

The suppression guard ignores a nonzero exit from find when output is consumed through process substitution.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a temporary PATH with a find shim that emits no output and exits 1, then run check-gitleaks-suppressions.sh against a disposable repository directory.

## Expected Behavior

Discovery errors make the guard fail. A clean successful traversal remains accepted and unmanaged Gitleaks files remain rejected.
acceptance_criteria: Check and propagate find errors from suppression/config discovery; a synthetic find executable that emits no results and exits nonzero must make the guard fail. Preserve current clean-tree and unmanaged-file rejection behavior.

close_reason: Suppression/config discovery now propagates find failures; the synthetic failing-find regression is in main commit 793c0315ec65f45dbf415bbb0e7a780be8e766ed (PR #18). The commit is an ancestor of current main 197ba24596d105971b4d0d88b2dfab3edd724156. Repository race tests, including internal/devsecops, pass at current main.

title: Propagate termination during cloud tool bootstrap
description:
## Problem

The bootstrap INT/TERM trap cleans state but does not terminate the script, allowing a canceled run to report success.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a disposable tools/cache root with a fake pinned Go executable that delays the first run. Send SIGTERM only to the bootstrap shell while the fake child is active, then allow the child to finish.

## Expected Behavior

The bootstrap exits nonzero, does not run later verification, keeps its lock while child work remains active, and cleans up after termination.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic fake Go command is signaled through a test that sends INT or TERM only to the bootstrap shell while the foreground child is active. The bootstrap must terminate with nonzero status, must not begin later verification, must retain the lock while work remains active, and must remove the lock after child cleanup.
close_reason: Signal/deadline cleanup for bootstrap child processes and helper groups, with regression coverage, merged in PR #19 at main commit 197ba24596d105971b4d0d88b2dfab3edd724156 after all 9 required checks passed. This closes only the cancellation bug; the parent bootstrap task remains open.
